prompt.context: Founded in 1984, your client, Pushman Potties, is a major US manufacturer of portable toilets, commonly referred to as "porta-potties". Pushman Potties' porta-potties are typically found in construction sites, agricultural fields, and other industrial settings. However, over the past several years sales of Pushman's standard porta-potties have stagnated, so the management team has approached your firm for help.
prompt.question: What are some potential avenues for revenue growth?

clarifying_info.a: Pushman's primary product is a standard industrial porta-potty. Several versions exist, but all are variants of the same base model.
Pushman has a broad footprint in the US. It serves all 50 states from regional offices in 32 states. Pushman currently has no international presence.
Pushman Potties are typically rented on a weekly or monthly basis. Maintenance is included in the rental agreement and is provided by Pushman.
In 2014, Pushman recorded approximately $650M in revenue, down from $670M in 2013.
Pushman has traditionally been the category leader in sales. Competitor financial information is not available.

exhibits.title: Number of Events/Year by US Region, 2013 and Pricing
exhibits.shows: A table of annual event counts by type (Weddings, Film Shoots, Festivals, Charity Events, Other Events) across five US regions (West, Midwest, NE, SE, SW); a bar chart showing average rental duration in days by event type; and a hypothesized pricing scheme based on rental duration.

framework: Existing customers / existing products: grow penetration and share in current industrial segments
Existing customers / new products: upsell current industrial clients on premium or specialty units
New customers / existing products: expand geography (international) or new verticals (events, festivals)
New customers / new products: enter luxury porta-potty segment targeting high-end events
Pricing levers: review rental rates vs. competitors, explore tiered pricing
Competitive landscape: assess whether competitors already serve luxury segment
Entry strategy: build (R&D new unit) vs. buy (acquire luxury PP operator) vs. partner
Risks: capital investment, brand dilution, demand cyclicality

questions.prompt: Prompt 1 – Revenue growth framework: What are potential avenues for revenue growth for Pushman Potties?
questions.guidance: Candidate should develop a MECE framework covering: existing vs. new customers, existing vs. new products (2x2 grid is ideal), pricing, competitive landscape, entry strategy (build/buy/partner), and risks. Candidate must focus on revenue, not profitability. If new products are not mentioned, interviewer should probe toward that direction.

questions.prompt: Prompt 2 – Market sizing: Pushman is primarily interested in entering the luxury porta-potty market. Such units feature running water (hot and cold), mirrors, lighting, and air conditioning. How would you approach estimating the size of the opportunity for such a product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first describe the approach before calculating. Steps: (1) brainstorm use cases (weddings, film shoots, festivals, high-end events); (2) recognize these units would be rented, not purchased; (3) identify drivers: total events per type, % requiring luxury PP, rental duration, units per event, price per day. After a logical approach is articulated, interviewer provides Exhibit 1. Candidate must then ask or be told the % of each event type requiring a luxury unit.

math.setup: Revenue = (total # of events) x (% requiring luxury PP) x (avg. rental duration in days) x (price per unit per day). Assume one unit per rental.
steps: Weddings: 1,850,000 total events x 2% = 37,000 rentals; duration <2 days -> price $1,500/day; assume 1 day -> 37,000 x 1 x $1,500 = $55.5M. Casebook uses 2 days: 37,000 x 2 x $1,500 = $111M
Film Shoots: (790+400+650+340+420)=2,600 events x 35% = 910 rentals; duration 3-4 days -> $1,300/day; assume 3 days: 910 x 3 x $1,300 = $3.55M. Casebook uses ~$4.5M (approx 3.8 days)
Charity Events: (350+140+380+280+250)=1,400 events x 25% = 350 rentals; <2 days -> $1,500/day; assume 1 day: 350 x 1 x $1,500 = $0.525M (~$1.4M with 2-day assumption)
math.answer: ~$124.6M total annual luxury porta-potty rental revenue opportunity; weddings account for roughly 90% of projected revenue

questions.prompt: Prompt 3 – Market entry considerations: Pushman believes this represents an attractive opportunity. What else should management consider in determining how best to enter the market?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover: (1) Competitive landscape — who already plays in luxury PP and what is their positioning; (2) Build vs. Buy — develop new unit internally or acquire an existing luxury PP operator; (3) Product economics — capex per unit, margin profile, break-even; (4) Risks — declining marriage rates, economic downturns reducing events, brand dilution of industrial brand moving upmarket, seasonality. After the candidate finishes, interviewer probes: 'Is there anything else the client should consider?'

brainstorming.prompt: What are potential use cases and customer segments for a luxury porta-potty?

recommendation: Recommend Pushman Potties pursue entry into the luxury porta-potty market
The addressable opportunity is approximately $124.6M annually, with weddings representing ~90% of projected revenue
Proposed entry strategy: evaluate a build vs. buy approach — acquiring an existing luxury PP operator may accelerate time-to-market and transfer operational know-how
risks: Declining or shifting marriage trends could erode the dominant wedding segment
Economic downturns reduce discretionary event spending and luxury rentals
Brand risk: Pushman's industrial brand may not resonate in the luxury events market
High capex per luxury unit with potentially longer payback periods
Seasonality: events are concentrated in spring/summer, creating revenue concentration
next_steps: Conduct competitive landscape analysis to identify existing luxury PP players and potential acquisition targets
Assess unit economics: capex per luxury unit, maintenance cost, target margin, and break-even volume
Develop a brand strategy (sub-brand vs. new brand) for the luxury segment
Pilot in one high-density region (e.g., Northeast) before national rollout
Establish partnerships with wedding planners and event coordinators as distribution channels
